---
title: "About EMMA"
---

EMMA is a decision-support tool for protected areas in South Africa’s Cape Floristic Region. It delivers continuously updated regional summaries and park-level reports on vegetation condition, anomalies, fire history, and veld age so managers can see what has changed and where to look next—co-developed with the South African Environmental Observation Network (SAEON) and academic partners at the University at Buffalo and the University of Cape Town.

To report a map or figure that looks wrong, or to suggest an improvement, see [Feedback](feedback.qmd).

## Project Workflow & Partners

Primary end-user and long-term steward: **SAEON**. The system informs protected-area managers and SAEON stakeholders including SANParks, CapeNature, and other conservation partners (e.g. WWF, The Nature Conservancy).

![Schematic of project workflow and partners](img/emma_workflow.png){fig-align="center"}

## Funding {#funding}

EMMA was supported by NASA award **80NSSC21K1183**, *Near-Real-Time Forecasting and Change Detection for a Fire-Prone Shrubland Ecosystem* (PI Adam M. Wilson, University at Buffalo; Co-Is Yingjie Hu, Jasper Slingsby, Glenn Moncrieff; period of performance 15 Sep 2020 – 14 Sep 2026). Primary end-user and long-term steward: **SAEON** (Eco-EMMA GitHub co-owned with University of Cape Town personnel). The system informs protected-area managers and SAEON stakeholders including SANParks, CapeNature, and other conservation partners.
